Alphabet key metrics — Search durability, ads moat, Cloud upside

GOOGL-zbar-2026-09-21 · USD · series 2026-09-22T02:14:51Z · built 2026-09-22 02:16 UTC

The short version

Alphabet is still an advertising company with a growing cloud attached. In the second quarter of 2026 revenue was $119.796 billion. Search & other was $63.271 billion (+16.8%), advertising $81.629 billion, and Google Cloud $24.768 billion (+81.8%). Paid clicks rose 13% while cost-per-click rose 3%. The falsifiers to watch are Search durability and ad-monetization quality — not whether Cloud had a good quarter. Trailing weekly PE on the latest complete week (W37) is about 16.86×. Official street forward PE on W38 is about 16.85× FY1 and 23.32× FY2, and the next-twelve-months multiple is blank.

The bet (opinion): Own Alphabet for three to ten years. The twin fear — that generative AI steals the Search front door, and that ads lose their personalization edge before AI monetizes — is the mispricing. The company still owns the distribution layer of the open web, the deepest consumer-intent catalog in advertising, and a cloud franchise that is finally printing real operating leverage. What would change the view first is a sustained loss of Search (and Gemini or the suite) as the default front door, or a break in ad monetization quality with no AI path to replace it. Cloud, YouTube, and Waymo are real upside — secondary to those two locks.

1. What Alphabet is and how it makes money

Alphabet’s cash engine is Google Services, and inside Services the engine is advertising: Search & other, YouTube ads, and Google Network. In Q2’26 those three summed to $81.629 billion of advertising — Search $63.271B, YouTube ads $11.055B, Network $7.303B. On top of ads, Services also includes subscriptions, platforms, and devices ($12.911B). Google Services in total was $94.540B. Google Cloud is reported separately ($24.768B). Other Bets remains a thin revenue line ($0.382B) and an operating-loss pocket.

The advertising chart is the composition picture — those three add to advertising. Stack or 100% only there. The window runs FY2021Q1 through FY2026Q2 and includes the fourth quarters of 2023, 2024, and 2025 as printed in the earnings letter. Those quarters are filled bars, not empty slots. An annual companion covers FY2022–FY2025.

Services versus Cloud versus Other Bets is the segment picture. Revenue, operating income, and net income sit on a later chart; they are not parts of one total.

Americas, EMEA, and APAC are a second composition, only where all three regions are printed. Incomplete quarters, including fourth quarters the letter does not break out this way, are left off the chart rather than drawn as empty slots. A small residual versus total company revenue is left out of that stack rather than invented as a fourth slice.

Services operating income in the quarter was $39.544 billion (margin about 42%). Cloud operating income was $8.814 billion (margin about 36%). Other Bets lost about $1.799 billion at the operating line. Consolidated operating income was $40.770 billion, margin about 34% — up versus a year earlier even as the company spends heavily on AI infrastructure.

Net income of $112.193 billion is not a clean run-rate. The quarter’s other income included a very large net gain on equity securities, on the order of $98 billion. Read operating income for the business; treat the net-income spike as a securities event that also inflates trailing earnings used in the PE.

2. Growth engine vs legacy core

Think of the stack as two stories that share one balance sheet and one AI research budget.

Legacy core — Search and the broader Services ads franchise. Still the majority of dollars and the primary thesis lock. Search’s share of advertising has drifted up (roughly the mid-70s toward the high-70s from 2024 into 2026), which is the opposite of a front-door abandonment print. In Q2’26 Search was about 77.5% of advertising. Network is the softer ads product line inside the core.

Growth engines — Cloud first; YouTube ads scale; Other Bets / Waymo as optionality. Cloud is the cleanest growth and margin-expansion story in the file. YouTube ads is a healthy second advertising franchise on the same consumer graph. Waymo sits inside Other Bets without a disclosed operating-KPI time series — real optionality, not yet a scoreboard.

These are editorial labels, not a rewrite of the segments. Search dollars against Cloud dollars sit side by side — not stacked as if they were one pie.

3. Walk the lines

3a. Search / front door + monetization

Search & other revenue by recent quarter (year over year):

  • 2024: roughly +12–14% through the year (Q1 +14.4%, Q2 +13.8%, Q3 +12.2%)
  • Early 2025: Q1’25 +9.8%, then Q2’25 +11.7%
  • Then stepped up: Q3’25 +14.5%, Q1’26 +19.1%, Q2’26 +16.8% to $63.271B

That is re-acceleration in the dollar line, not a sustained loss of the front door.

MD&A monetization is year-over-year percentages only. Absolute RPM is not invented.

  • 2024 pattern: high cost-per-click, softer clicks (CPC often +7–8%, clicks +4–6%)
  • Into 2026: high clicks, cooler CPC — Q1’26 clicks +13%, CPC +5%; Q2’26 clicks +13%, CPC +3%

Volume is carrying Search dollars while unit-price growth cooled versus the 2024–25 band. That is the live monetization-quality lens on the primary falsifier. Gemini app usage and AI Overviews monetization are discussed on earnings calls but are not published as a durable quarterly series we can chart.

Clicks and cost-per-click sit side by side as two percentages — not one stack.

3b. Ads suite / Network / TAC

Network revenue Q2’26 was $7.303B versus $7.354B a year earlier (−0.7%). Network impressions have been negative year over year for a long stretch. Q2’26 impressions were −12% with cost-per-impression +13% — price covering volume loss. If the personalization moat were breaking in the third-party channel, this is where the bruise shows first. It is soft, not yet a company-level collapse.

Traffic acquisition costs in Q2’26 were $16.179B, about 19.8% of advertising — down a bit versus about 20.6% a year earlier. Full-year TAC: FY2022 $48.955B (22.0% of ads), FY2023 $50.886B (21.4%), FY2024 $54.900B (20.7%), FY2025 $59.926B (20.3%). Dollars up, rate gently down — not a TAC blow-up.

TAC dollars and the TAC rate travel on separate panels. They are not stacked, and they do not share one axis.

3c. YouTube

YouTube ads in Q2’26 were $11.055B, +12.9% year over year. Secondary watch under the locked thesis — healthy growth, not the primary falsifier. It sits in the advertising stack with Search and Network; treat it as scale on the same consumer graph rather than a separate company.

3d. Cloud

Google Cloud Q2’26 revenue was $24.768B, +81.8% versus $13.624B a year earlier. Operating income was $8.814B, margin about 35.6%, versus $2.826B / ~20.7% in Q2’25. This is the growth and profitability surge on the secondary engine. It must not bury the Search and ads locks in the narrative — but it is allowed to sit on the scoreboard as upside.

Cloud revenue and Cloud operating income sit side by side. They are not additive layers.

Services, Cloud, and Other Bets operating income are the same idea at segment level. Other Bets is a loss, so this chart is grouped only.

3e. Other Bets / Waymo

Other Bets revenue in Q2’26 was $0.382B; the operating loss was about $1.799B. Waymo operating metrics — paid trips, utilization, markets live — are not disclosed as a durable quarterly series. Optionality without a scoreboard: say so honestly. There is no Waymo KPI chart built from press anecdotes.

4. Unit economics → valuation

Operating trajectory first. Quarterly revenue in Q2’26 was $119.796B (+24%); operating income $40.770B (+30%); operating margin about 34%. CapEx is the swing factor in cash.

Q2’26 operating cash flow was $39.1B, CapEx $44.9B, free cash flow −$5.8B on the quarterly window — the first clear quarterly deficit in the recent stretch as AI infrastructure spend overtakes cash from operations. Q1’26 still printed free cash flow of about +$10.1B. The quarterly chart is the quarter window only, and only quarters where operating cash flow, CapEx, and free cash flow are all printed. Fourth-quarter cash is omitted, not drawn as an empty slot and not plugged from the full year.

Full-year 2025 free cash flow was $73.266B on $91.447B of CapEx and $164.713B of operating cash flow. That annual picture stays on its own chart. The old nine-month stub from 2015 is not mixed in.

Where the multiple sits. Price on one chart. Trailing PE on another. No dual axis.

6. Open gaps

  • Gemini / AI Overviews monetization and query share — call color only; no durable disclosed series for front-door product mix.
  • Absolute RPM / CPC dollars — the MD&A gives year-over-year percent only.
  • Waymo operating KPIs (trips, paid miles, cities, utilization) — absent.
  • Monetization and quarterly cash fourth quarters — clicks, CPC, and quarterly free cash flow still skip FY2023Q4, FY2024Q4, and FY2025Q4. Product, segment operating income, and TAC for those quarters are letter prints on their charts.
  • Forward PE history — weeks before W38 stay blank. They are not backfilled.
  • Next-twelve-months forward PE — blank.
  • Clean trailing earnings for PE — trailing net income includes the large 2026 securities gains. There is no ex-items series to swap in silently.
  • Advertising take-rate versus the industry — not in the extracted series.
  • Cloud backlog as a long quarterly KPI — letter color only, where it is not yet a series in this file.
  • Pre-2023 dense Services and Cloud operating income — the usable chart window starts cleanly at FY2023Q1.
Method & definitional notes
  • Q1–Q2’26 net income is distorted by large equity-securities gains (about $98 billion in Q2’26). Read operating income for the business. Trailing earnings used in PE inherit that gain.
  • FY2023Q4, FY2024Q4, and FY2025Q4 product, segment operating income, and TAC are Exhibit 99.1 letter prints. Monetization year-over-year and quarterly cash skip those fourth quarters — the periods are omitted, not drawn as empty slots.
  • Income statement Q4 quarters are residual extracts already in the file (labeled). That rule does not extend to product lines. Product fourth quarters on the charts are letter prints, not residuals.
  • Weekly trailing PE runs through complete week W37 (ending 2026-09-13, about 16.86×). W38 is the forward print only and is not on the trailing chart. NTM is blank. FY2 PE above FY1 is mechanical because street FY2 earnings sit below FY1.
  • Quarterly free cash flow and full-year free cash flow are separate charts. The FY2015 nine-month stub is not on the annual chart.
  • Absolute RPM and CPC dollars are not in the file. Waymo operating KPIs are not in the file. Forward PE before W38 is not backfilled.
